newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy's Consob refers inside trade cases to courts.
newsitem.headline: Italy's Consob refers inside trade cases to courts.

text.p: Italian stock market regulator Consob said it had decided to refer three cases of suspected insider trading to magistrates for possible investigation.
Under Italian law, Consob must send its findings to magistrates and the magistrates then decide whether to pursue the investigations.

Consob said in a statement the first case, which had been sent to magistrates in the northwest city of Turin, related to trading operations on shares in the Credito Romagnolo banking group carried out before October 26, 1994.
Consob said "on that date the board of Credito Italiano bank said it planned to launch a public buy offer (OPV) for a 48.26 percent stake in Credito Romagnolo."

The second case, which had been passed to magistrates in Milan, dealt with alleged illicit use of "confidential information" in relation to trading operations in shares in investment bank Euromobiliare before February 17, 1994.

Consob's checks concerned the period preceding newspaper reports of rumours of the possible sale of a 56.61 percent controlling stake in Euromobiliare held by Britain's Midland Bank to Credito Emiliano through Samuel Montague International Holdings of London.

The third case, which had gone to magistrates in the northeast city of Trieste, concerned alleged illicit use of "confidential information" and manipulative practices in trading of shares in Tripcovich and Gottardo Ruffoni between November 1, 1993 and May 20, 1994, when Tripcovich announced problems in many of its companies.
